page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-8 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the c4d server family. It is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture and 31.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistent disk volumes.

Operating with dedicated CPU allocation, the c4d-standard-8 provides consistent compute performance without the resource contention typical of shared-core or burstable instances. The balanced allocation of 3.88 GB of memory per vCPU positions this instance as a standard general-purpose resource. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the lack of bundled local storage and GPU accelerators minimizes baseline infrastructure overhead, making it a predictable option for workloads that do not require high-speed local scratch space or hardware acceleration.

This instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, application servers, microservices, and moderate database hosting. It is also appropriate for development environments, containerized applications, and basic multi-threaded processing tasks that fit within its 31.0 GB memory footprint.
